scope.boundary: Prepare the intended stable release, qualify its exact artifacts, publish with candidate-specific approval, and report or recover honestly.
scope.coverage_claim: Outcome-driven scenarios cover the 24 recurring Release requirements; REL-SR-20/21 retain their original scoped source-consolidation obligations outside this recurring catalog. Linked methods provide supporting realization; native discovery owns the full executable inventory and no per-method catalog entry is required. Partial/proposed proof remains explicit. Local fixture and candidate checks do not establish live publication or hosted authorization.

fixture_rules.isolation: Each executable case and variant owns its temporary root, mutable mappings and logs, with cleanup registered immediately. Review procedures identify their exact reviewed subjects without changing publication state.
fixture_rules.independent_expectations: Author expected versions, row labels and diagnostics here from Release obligations. Capture preservation baselines before actions. Do not compute expected values with the production transformation.
fixture_rules.negative_setup: Establish a valid prepared baseline before the defining mutation. Mutation must change the intended field; a rejection caused only by another fixture defect does not realize the case.
fixture_rules.version_roles: Each group declares synthetic previous/target roles: preparation commonly uses 0.3.4/0.3.5, candidate fixtures 0.5.0/0.5.1, and checklist fixtures 1.2.3. A new release alone does not add cases or require renumbering; real candidate integration uses its actual selected artifacts.
fixture_rules.resource_boundary: All root-relative paths in given/when/then refer to the private fixture root. Catalog references in owner/target/realization refer to the repository. No public publication is performed.
